top5.title: Anthropic’s IPO reaches record highs
top5.description: Anthropic’s stock jumped 34% at the open before ending the day up 17%. The company raised 81 billion dollars in its IPO, bringing the total raised to 107.3 billion with its private placement.
top5.why: Anthropic’s record IPO puts a major market valuation on the AI boom and could reset expectations for the financing and profitability of frontier-model companies.

top5.title: U.S. restricts exports of AI chips to foreign data centers
top5.description: The U.S. Commerce Department restricted, effective November 19, exports of advanced AI chips to foreign data centers providing large-scale computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted countries.
top5.why: New U.S. restrictions on AI-chip exports to foreign data centers materially tighten access to computing capacity and raise compliance risks for global cloud and semiconductor companies.

top5.title: Data center electricity consumption could double by 2030
top5.description: According to the International Energy Agency, data centers will consume twice as much electricity in 2030, with AI accounting for three-quarters of the increase. The sector’s carbon emissions could rise by 70% in four years.
top5.why: The projected doubling of data-center electricity demand by 2030 makes power availability, grid investment, and carbon costs central constraints on AI expansion.

top5.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a faster AI model
top5.description: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon on its paid API, Gemini app, and development tools. The company says it is three times faster than Gemini 4 Carbon and outperforms Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on a reasoning benchmark.
top5.why: Google’s launch of Gemini 4 Neon intensifies competition among frontier-model providers and signals continued pressure on performance, speed, and API pricing.

top5.title: Microsoft’s official Python framework for agents hijacked to spread malware
top5.description: Microsoft’s official Python framework for agents was compromised to distribute malicious software.
top5.why: The compromise of Microsoft’s official agent framework to distribute malware highlights a serious new supply-chain risk as enterprises rapidly adopt AI-agent software.
